column4: Pixel-art game character sprite in exactly the same style as the reference image: same pixel size, same palette, same shading, front view, full body standing, feet touching the bottom edge, character centred and filling about 90% of the height. It is the same young woman from the reference, but something is deeply wrong with her, in a quiet way, like a found 1990s horror game: grey-blue skin, the same black dress now soaked and darker, wet hair hanging over half of her face, arms a little too long hanging straight down, one shoe missing, mud on her legs, her eyes are two tiny white dots, no visible mouth, no cigarette, no handbag. Perfectly still, standing straight, facing the viewer. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around her, no ground shadow, no floor, no text, no border, no watermark.

Seamless tileable texture, flat orthographic view filling the whole square, no perspective: the inside wall of an old concrete sewer pipe in a 1970s Eastern European summer camp. Wet grey concrete with formwork seams, dark water stains running down, rust streaks from old bolts, patches of green-black slime, a few hairline cracks. Low saturation, slightly dark, gritty, in the style of 1990s Build-engine game textures (Duke Nukem 3D, Redneck Rampage), crisp, no text, no border, must tile seamlessly on all four edges.

A blank sheet of old yellowed paper lying flat, seen straight from above, filling the entire canvas edge to edge: faint pale blue graph-paper grid, creases from being folded in four, a brown coffee-ring stain in one corner, small water damage spots, smudged pencil eraser marks, slightly dirty edges. Nothing written on it, no text, no lines drawn except the faint grid, no objects on top of it, no table visible, no border.

A faded amateur colour photograph from summer 1987, taken with a cheap Eastern European film camera: a group of about fifteen children and two adult camp leaders posing in front of small wooden cabins at the edge of a dark lake in a Czech pine forest, late evening light, the colours shifted to orange and cyan, film grain, slight blur, a light leak in one corner, a scratched print scanned on a cheap 1990s flatbed scanner. At the far left edge, half in the trees and slightly out of focus, a tall man in a long dark coat and a hat stands facing the camera; nobody in the group looks at him. One small girl in red sandals stands a little apart from the others at the edge of the group, her face blurred as if she moved. No text, no watermark, no borders.
